He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton Bluejays]]. He was drafted 38th overall by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in the [[2018 NBA draft]] and then traded to the [[Detroit Pistons]]. ==Early life== Thomas attended [[Omaha Benson High School Magnet]] in [[Omaha, Nebraska]]. He committed to [[Creighton University]] to play [[college basketball]].{{cite web|url=http://www.omaha.com/creighton/former-benson-all-stater-khyri-thomas-signs-with-jays/article_76927784-9377-506c-b15c-aaeabc03c3bc.html|title=Former Benson all-stater Khyri Thomas signs with Jays | Creighton|website=omaha.com|access-date=April 7, 2018}} Prior to attending Creighton, he attended [[Fork Union Military Academy]].{{cite web|url=http://www.omaha.com/creighton/former-benson-star-all-nebraska-captain-thomas-coming-home-to/article_60a86954-b2d2-11e4-b877-77028e086fcf.html|title=Former Benson star, All-Nebraska captain Thomas coming home to play for CU | Creighton|website=omaha.com|access-date=April 7, 2018}} ==College career== As a freshman at Creighton, Thomas averaged 6.2 points, 1.4 assists and 3.7 rebounds per game. As a sophomore, he averaged 12.3 points, 3.3 assists and 5.8 rebounds and was named the Big East Defensive Player of the Year along with [[Josh Hart (basketball)|Josh Hart]] and [[Mikal Bridges]].{{cite web|url=http://www.omaha.com/creighton/mens-basketball/khyri-thomas-shares-league-s-defensive-player-of-the-year/article_e916b8e8-027d-11e7-ac80-aff6af38e62d.html|title=Khyri Thomas shares league's defensive player of the year award with two others | Men's Basketball|website=omaha.com|access-date=April 7, 2018}} As a junior, he averaged 15.1 points, 2.8 assists and 4.4 rebounds and again was named the Big East Defensive Player of the Year.{{cite web|url=http://www.omaha.com/creighton/blog/khyri-thomas-named-big-east-defensive-player-of-the-year/article_4c812c7a-2086-11e8-84b6-132055c07dff.html|title=Khyri Thomas named Big East defensive player of the year (again) | Blog|website=omaha.com|access-date=April 7, 2018}} He entered the [[2018 NBA draft]] without initially hiring an agent, but on May 13 announced he was staying in the draft and forfeiting his final season at Creighton.{{cite news|last1=Johnson|first1=Raphielle|title=Creighton guard Khyri Thomas to remain in 2018 NBA Draft|url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2018/05/13/creighton-guard-khyri-thomas-to-remain-in-2018-nba-draft/|access-date=May 14, 2018|work=[[NBC Sports]]|date=May 13, 2018}} ==Professional career== ===Detroit Pistons (2018–2020)=== On June 21, 2018, Thomas was drafted 38th overall by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in the [[2018 NBA draft]]. He was then traded to the [[Detroit Pistons]] in exchange for two future second-round draft picks.{{cite news|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/nba/pistons/2018/06/21/detroit-pistons-2018-nba-draft/720696002/ |title=Detroit Pistons get Khyri Thomas in trade with 76ers, add Bruce Brown |newspaper=[[Detroit Free Press]]|first=Marlowe |last=Alter |date=June 21, 2018 |access-date=June 21, 2018}} Thomas made his NBA debut on November 9, 2018, against the [[Atlanta Hawks]], playing four minutes and making a three pointer.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/features/no-slow-start-time-around-pistons-blow-out-hawks|title=No slow start this time around as Pistons blow out Hawks|first=Keith|last=Langlois|work=Pistons.com|date=November 9, 2018|access-date=December 4, 2018}} On November 20, 2020, the Pistons traded Thomas to the Atlanta Hawks; he was waived shortly after.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/atlanta-hawks-acquire-tony-snell-detroit-pistons|title=Atlanta Hawks Acquire Tony Snell from Detroit Pistons|work=NBA.com|date=November 20, 2020}} ===Austin Spurs (2021)=== On December 13, 2020, Thomas was reported to have had signed with and waived by the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite web|first1=JD|last1=Shaw|title=Spurs Sign, Waive Khyri Thomas|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2020/12/spurs-sign-waive-khyri-thomas.html|date=December 13, 2020 |website=hoopsrumors.com|access-date=December 14, 2020}} He was later included in roster of [[Austin Spurs]]{{cite web|title=Austin Spurs announce 2021 roster|url=https://austin.gleague.nba.com/news/austin-spurs-announce-2021-roster|date=February 1, 2021|website=NBA.com|accessdate=February 1, 2021}} where he appeared in seven games and averaged 13.9 points, 3.4 rebounds and 2.3 three-pointers made on 45.7% shooting, which was the fourth-highest three-point percentage of any player who averaged at least 2.0 three pointers with two or more games played.{{cite web|title=Rockets Sign Khyri Thomas to 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-sign-khyri-thomas-10-day-contract|date=May 7, 2021|website=NBA.com|accessdate=May 7, 2021}} ===Houston Rockets (2021)=== On May 7, 2021, Thomas signed a 10-day contract with the [[Houston Rockets]]. In his first two days on this contract, he averaged 21.5 points on 57.1% shooting.{{cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/31411362/nba-power-rankings-races-players-watching-closely-final-week |author= |date=10 May 2021 |title=NBA Power Rankings: The races and players we're watching closely in the final week |work=[[ESPN]] |access-date=10 May 2021}} On May 8, 2021, Thomas scored a career-high 27 points with five rebounds, five steals, three assists and two blocks in a 116–124 loss to the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401307823|title=NBA-leading Jazz beat Rockets 124-116 for 50th victory|date=May 8, 2021|website=ESPN.com|accessdate=May 8, 2021}} On May 14, he signed a multi-year contract with the Rockets.{{cite web|title=Rockets Announce Roster Transactions|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-announce-roster-transactions|date=May 14, 2021|website=NBA.com|accessdate=May 14, 2021}} However, he was waived on October 6.{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Rockets Waive Khyri Thomas To Complete Trade With Nets|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2021/10/rockets-waive-khyri-thomas-to-complete-trade-with-nets.html|date=October 6, 2021|website=HoopsRumors.com|accessdate=October 6, 2021}} ===Bilbao Basket (2021–2022)=== On November 24, 2021, Thomas signed with [[Bilbao Basket]] of the [[Liga ACB]].{{cite web|title=El escolta norteamericano Khyri Thomas firma con Surne Bilbao|url=https://www.bilbaobasket.biz/el-escolta-norteamericano-khyri-thomas-firma-con-surne-bilbao-basket/|website=BilbaoBasket.biz|date=November 24, 2021|access-date=November 24, 2021|language=Spanish}} He played only two games for the team.{{Cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Khyri-Thomas/Summary/84388|title=Khyri Thomas Player Profile, Houston Rockets, News, Rumors, NBA Stats, NCAA Stats, G League Stats, International Stats, Game Logs, Bests, Awards - RealGM|website=basketball.realgm.com}} ===Maccabi Tel Aviv (2022)=== On January 10, 2022, Thomas signed with [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]] and the [[EuroLeague]].{{Cite web|title=Maccabi signed Khyri Thomas|url=http://maccabi.co.il/news.asp?id=8659&lang=en|access-date=January 10, 2022|website=Maccabi Tel Aviv}} ===Tofaş (2022)=== On July 15, 2022, he has signed with [[Tofaş S.K.|Tofaş]] of [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).{{Cite web|url=http://tofasspor.com/haber-2559-khyri_thomas_tofasta|title=Khyri Thomas Tofaş'ta|last=|first=|date=July 15, 2022|website=tofasspor.com|publisher=|language=tr|access-date=August 5, 2022}} In October 2022, after playing only two games with his new club, he decided to give a break to his professional career for personal reasons.{{Cite web|url=http://tofasspor.com/haber-2624-khyri_thomas_hakkinda_bilgilendirme|title=Khyri Thomas Hakkında Bilgilendirme;|last=|first=|date=October 14, 2022|website=|publisher=[[Tofaş S.K.|Tofaş]]|language=tr|access-date=October 15, 2022}} ===Petkim Spor (2023–2024)=== On July 25, 2023, he signed with [[Petkim Spor]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).{{Cite tweet |user=Petkimspor |number=1683896601545146370 |title=Ailemize hoş geldin Khyri Thomas}} === Calgary Surge (2025) === On March 24, 2025, Thomas signed a one-year contract with the [[Calgary Surge]] of the [[Canadian Elite Basketball League]]. He was the first player to sign with the team for the 2025 season.{{Cite news |title=Calgary Surge Sign Former NBA Draft Pick Khyri Thomas
